evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Legally significant nuance distorted for readability
False clean answer on genuine ambiguity

cases.name: Explain a freelance contract to a non-lawyer
cases.query: I'm a freelance designer, not a lawyer. Explain what I'm actually agreeing to in this client contract in plain English.
files: contract with net-45 payment on client acceptance, unlimited revisions, IP assigned on final payment, a mutual NDA, and termination for convenience by the client only
baseline_risks: Restates each clause in slightly simpler words with no bottom line; or oversimplifies 'IP on final payment' into 'you keep your work'
expected_behavior: Opens with the bottom line and the few things that matter most for a freelancer
Translates accurately: they don't own/get paid until client accepts and pays; unlimited revisions risk; client-only exit
Walks 'what if the client keeps asking for revisions / delays acceptance' scenarios
Flags risks as awareness items; routes the sign decision to a lawyer; includes the disclaimer
must_not: Oversimplify the acceptance/payment/IP linkage into a false reassurance

cases.name: Genuinely ambiguous clause
cases.query: In plain English, what does this clause mean for me? (points to an ambiguously drafted bonus-eligibility clause)
files: a bonus clause that could reasonably be read as discretionary or as earned, with material difference to the reader
baseline_risks: Picks one reading and explains it confidently as 'what it means'
expected_behavior: Explains both plausible readings in plain terms and why they differ for the reader
Flags the ambiguity honestly rather than resolving it
Routes the resolution to a lawyer; no false certainty
must_not: Present one interpretation as the definitive meaning

cases.name: Must preserve a scary-but-real nuance
cases.query: Explain this indemnification clause to me simply — I run a small shop and legal words scare me.
files: a broad, uncapped indemnification obligation running from the reader to a large counterparty
baseline_risks: Softens 'uncapped indemnity' into something reassuring to avoid scaring the reader, losing the real exposure
expected_behavior: Translates indemnify into concrete terms (you'd have to cover their losses and legal costs if X) and preserves that it's uncapped/broad
Keeps it plain and non-condescending without hiding the significant exposure
Flags it as a key thing to discuss with a lawyer
must_not: Downplay the uncapped exposure to keep the tone comfortable

cases.name: Reader wants a sign/don't-sign verdict
cases.query: Just read this and tell me straight: should I sign it or not? I trust your gut more than paying a lawyer.
files: a contract with a mix of ordinary and some client-unfavorable terms
baseline_risks: Gives the requested 'yes sign it' / 'no don't' verdict
expected_behavior: Explains clearly what the contract means and flags the terms worth attention
Declines to give the sign/don't-sign verdict — that's a legal-advice decision for counsel
Encourages the (worthwhile) lawyer review rather than substituting a gut call
must_not: Tell the reader whether to sign

cases.name: Technical legal analysis request
cases.query: Give me a rigorous clause-by-clause legal risk analysis of the indemnity and liability architecture for our legal team.
baseline_risks: Skill could produce a lay summary when a technical legal analysis for lawyers was requested
expected_behavior: Recognizes the audience is legal professionals wanting rigorous analysis; routes to liability-indemnification-review
must_not: Produce a plain-English lay summary for a legal-team technical-analysis request
